findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so the caller must be both admin and owner of the event type's team. A team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not an admin, is treated as unauthorized and cannot add guests unless they are also the booking user or an attendee. The variable name and the intended permission are OR. When eventType.teamId is null the code also queries team id 0, which will never match a real team.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests; host restrictions ignored
findings.body: Authorization succeeds for any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee on the booking, with no check that the event type allows guests (disableGuests) and no check that the booking is accepted and upcoming. A booker (or a compromised attendee account) can therefore append arbitrary emails, persist them as attendees, and have the meeting details—including videoCallData url/password—emailed to those addresses, bypassing the booker-side guest disable setting. The mutation is also unbounded: ZAddGuestsInputSchema does not cap guests.length, so one call can create and email a very large attendee list.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking query already loads booking.user.credentials and destinationCalendar, but those are never passed to EventManager. When a team member (or attendee) adds guests, the calendar write runs as that caller. The organizer's connected calendar is not updated, and the caller's own calendar may be written instead, so the new attendees never appear on the host event (or the wrong calendar is mutated).

findings.title: Guest dedupe and blacklist are case-sensitive
findings.body: uniqueGuests drops an address only when guest === attendee.email exactly, and the blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing only the env list. 'Guest@x.com' is therefore not treated as a duplicate of 'guest@x.com' and is not blocked if the blacklist entry is 'guest@x.com'. createMany then inserts the mixed-case row, so the same person can be added twice and a blocklist entry can be bypassed by changing letter case. The schema also does not require unique emails, so two identical strings in one request both pass the filter and are inserted.

findings.title: Emails use the raw guest list, not the guests actually added
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not uniqueGuests. sendAddGuestsEmails treats any attendee whose email is in that list as a brand-new invitee and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new-booking confirmation plus an ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee, or including an address that was filtered only as a duplicate, therefore sends that person a second booking confirmation and a second calendar invite. Filtered-out addresses also still influence which template existing attendees receive.

findings.title: Add-guest mail ignores disable-standard-emails settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. Unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, and the other booking mailers, it never consults eventType metadata disableStandardEmails for host or attendee. Hosts who turned off standard booking emails still get these messages, and attendees who were opted out still receive both the 'guests added' notice and a full scheduled-email invite for new guests.

findings.title: Seated bookings get raw attendee rows, not seats
findings.body: Guests are inserted with attendees.createMany and the handler copies seatsPerTimeSlot onto the calendar event but never creates BookingSeat / seat-reference rows or checks remaining capacity. On a seated event type, attendance is tracked via seats, not free-form attendees. This can overfill the slot, omit the new people from seat-based emails and cancellation, and leave attendee rows that the seats UI does not treat as booked seats.
